criteria.reasoning: The brief states "Ask Amount: $80,000 (single figure, not a range)" and the talking points propose "an anonymous investment of $80,000". No other ask figure or range is given.

It identifies the "Largest single household gift: $20,000 (2025-10-14 DAF grant)" from the Vandermolen Family Fund, excludes the $25,000 corporate gala sponsorship under Section 1.5, and computes "4 × $20,000 = $80,000" as the cap applied to the $95,000 formula figure.

The program priority is "Adult Literacy Program" with options of the Upriver evening site, Tutor Corps/learner materials, or the Adult Literacy Endowment. It explicitly says "no capital or naming components (such as the $75,000 Adult Literacy Learning Lab) will be proposed", so no Open Doors option is offered.

No naming opportunity is offered; the brief cites Policy A5 that "naming opportunities are never offered to donors requesting anonymity" and instructs solicitors not to raise "capital naming spaces, or the Adult Literacy Learning Lab".

Recognition is "100% Anonymous"; under A4 the gift "is not listed in annual reports, on donor walls, or in public announcements, and is acknowledged strictly by private letter", and follow-up is a "formal, private thank-you letter". The CRM recognition name is not used for the gift.
"Primary Prospect Asked: Celeste Vandermolen (with Martin Vandermolen present)", citing Section 4 and Martin's statement that Celeste runs their giving decisions.

The meeting is arranged by Teresa emailing Celeste "at celeste.vdm@example.net" (or home phone) and held "at their home, 1418 Cormorant Lane". The company line, vandermolenmarine.com emails and 220 Harbor Way appear only as explicit prohibitions.

The solicitation team is "Relationship Manager: Teresa Lindahl" and "Leadership Partner: Lillian Cho, Board of Directors", justified by Celeste's request and her FY27 gift. Dr. Hartley appears only as a signer of the thank-you letter, which the criterion permits; Hale is disqualified.
The brief says Hale "is strictly disqualified under Section 4 of the Conflict of Interest Policy" due to the arbitration, and gives him no role in cultivation or solicitation.

The talking-points section names the gift outright: "The Rasmussen family's anonymous $100,000 gift to the Adult Literacy Endowment closed in August 2026; it must not be mentioned to Celeste or Martin." Even framed as a prohibition, the brief discloses the family's name, the amount and purpose, which the criterion says fails in any form.

Timing is "November 2026", after the mid-October advisor meeting, with Teresa emailing Celeste "In late October 2026 (confirming their financial advisor meeting has concluded)" only to coordinate the November visit.

The donor facts stated (giving history, $382,000 capacity, inclination 4, tutoring since 2023, anonymity requests, advisor timing, the request for Lillian Cho, contact preferences) all trace to the contact reports, CRM record and research profile. Minor paraphrase (e.g., framing "Their giving goes to adult literacy" within Celeste's quote) reflects content in the files and introduces no unsourced fact about the donors.
